mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the next 20-day periods following any FEDFUNDS observation below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 9.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the next 5-day periods when UNRATE exceeds 9.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate weak aggregate demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate profit expectations.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST decline from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the next 60-day periods when both RSAFS and HOUST decline from their prior month values.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (above 2.0% annualized), manufacturing output expansion supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the next 20-day periods when INDPRO growth rate exceeds 2.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 2.5% annualized signals rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the Federal Reserve may tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the next 5-day periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (above 100,000 jobs per month) signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the next 20-day periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong consumer spending (RSAFS above 380,000 million dollars), retail sales growth supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the next 60-day periods when RSAFS exceeds 380,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 90.0 (index, 2017=100) signals a manufacturing slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate output and profits contract.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the next 5-day periods when INDPRO is below 90.0.
